out.other_title: Short snippets, high hallucination rate; single critique may be weaker than debate
out.rationale: McAleese et al. suggest a single critique step may be weaker than multi-step procedures such as consultancy or debate. Hammond and Adam-Day compare protocols on APPS code validation and report stabilised expert iteration improves every protocol's worst-case performance with debate performing particularly well; verifiers are GPT-4o-mini models, not human contractors, and code snippets are APPS solutions. The cited passages include no single-critique protocol, so Hammond and Adam-Day's result does not bear on McAleese et al.'s claim, and McAleese et al.'s limitation does not bear on Hammond and Adam-Day's result.
out.scope: proposed SHARES_TOPIC: multi-step interactive protocols such as debate for checking code, in McAleese et al.'s limitation that a single critique may be weaker than such procedures and in Hammond and Adam-Day's comparison of protocols on APPS code validation

text: The paper reports that debate and the solo verifier have high precision-to-recall ratios because vanilla expert iteration amplifies an initially low acceptance rate. 'Stabilised' expert iteration, which replaces the verifier's guess with the true label in an annealed share of rollouts, reduces this mode collapse, has a small mixed effect on protocols' mean accuracy, and improves every protocol's worst-case performance, with debate performing particularly well.
title: Stabilised expert iteration improves worst-case performance; debate does particularly well
